issues.description: The problem statement and task text refer to a Farm method named printFarmSong(), but both the template and the solution implement and reference a method named singFarmSong(). This name mismatch between the specification and provided code will confuse students (they may implement printFarmSong() while the provided template and tests expect singFarmSong()), preventing straightforward implementation and testing of the song functionality.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either change the problem statement and task descriptions to refer to singFarmSong(), or rename the method in the template and solution to printFarmSong(). Update any references in Main, UML, and tests accordingly so all artifacts use the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Farm method named printFarmSong(), but both the template and the reference solution define and use singFarmSong() instead. This naming mismatch for the same conceptual operation (playing/printing the farm song) can confuse students about which method to implement or call and creates a direct mapping barrier between the written requirements and the provided code.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Either (A) rename singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() in the template and solution Farm.java (and update all calls, e.g., Main) to match the problem statement and UML; or (B) update the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong() consistently. Prefer option A to align code with the documented requirement.
